career_spells.employer: Society of the Catholic Apostolate (Pallottines), Victoria
career_spells.evidence_note: Wallace told ABC that he entered a Pallottine monastery at age 19 and left about eight months later. No evidence identifies this religious formation as paid employment.
career_spells.counting_note: Religious formation or study is excluded.

career_spells.evidence_note: The Parliamentary Handbook begins Wallace's carpenter-and-joiner/builder chronology in 1987. His official biography and ABC profile say his mother arranged an apprenticeship after he left the monastery and that he completed the trade. The employer, exact dates, hours and leave are not published. Later first-person speech locates apprenticeship on Melbourne high-rise commercial construction site and recalls around1986or1987; existing1987officialyear retained with approximate recollection noted. BLF membership is not union employment.
career_spells.counting_note: Private employment is supported, but employer identity and the evidence needed for a full-time calculation are missing.

career_spells.employer: Self-employed subcontract carpentry and building business, entity not identified
career_spells.role: Subcontract carpenter, builder and business owner
career_spells.evidence_note: Official and first-person sources say Wallace became a subcontract carpenter, then a builder and owner of his own business for about a decade before qualifying as a barrister in 2000. The Parliamentary Handbook records carpenter-and-joiner/builder activity through 2016, creating an unresolved overlap with legal practice; no business name, licence history or exact boundaries are supplied. Undated chambers profile lists registered-builder QBCClicence47895. Licence holding alone does not prove continuing paid building activity. Previously encoded2000cessation was an assumed transition and is removed pending resolution ofofficial2016overlap.
career_spells.counting_note: Substantive private self-employment is supported, but exact dates, workload, leave and the possible post-2000 continuation cannot be resolved.

career_spells.evidence_note: Wallace's official biography says he completed his QUT law degree in his late twenties while operating his building business; in Parliament he described the study as full-time. The commencement and graduation dates are not published in the sources reviewed, while admission to the bar is reported in 2000. ABC2016electionguide explicitly gives1997–2000lawstudy; retained as secondary year-precision boundaries,not inferred from baradmission.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded; its overlap with the building business remains relevant to workload evidence.

career_spells.employer: Self-employed legal practice; Alfred Lutwyche Chambers / Inns of Court Sunshine Coast affiliation
career_spells.evidence_note: The Parliamentary Handbook records barrister practice from 2000 to 2016. Wallace repeatedly described the interval as the 16 years immediately before election, and his official biography says his own practice was based in Maroochydore. Exact admission, first-brief, cessation, hours, leave and the nature of any continuing building business are not supplied. Primary chambers profile names SunshineCoastInns ofCourt and registered-adjudicator status; Minister2014also describes adjudication experience. Chambers are professional affiliation,not assumed employer. Unsupported exact election-day cessation reduced toofficial2016year; undatedprofile doesnot prove post-election work.
career_spells.counting_note: Private self-employment is established but cannot be converted to full-time years without workload, leave and exact boundary evidence.

career_spells.employer: Self-employed legal practice — Queensland Government/QBCC clients
career_spells.role: Independent construction-law reviewer and report author
career_spells.evidence_note: In Parliament Wallace said that as a barrister he produced three independent reports for the Queensland Government between 2013 and 2015 concerning building-regulation reform, security of payment and private certification. This is recorded as client work within legal practice, not separate public-service employment. Paymentsreview appointment21December2012 explicitly stated in2014evidence; reportdelivered24May2013. May2013governmentresponse identifies separateQBSApanel membership. QBCCcommissioned BuildingAct/certificationreview in2014,followed byconsultation toJanuary2015. These refine umbrella clientwork,not continuous full-time governmentemployment.2015end retained only as broadfirst-personreport interval,not precise contractcessation.
career_spells.counting_note: Private self-employed provider; publicclientdoesnottransferemployercontrol. Entirely nested within legalpractice spell; no duplicateheadlineyears.

career_spells.employer: Alexandra Headland Surf Life Saving Club
career_spells.role: Honorary secretary, vice-president, patrol captain and emergency-response volunteer
career_spells.evidence_note: Wallace's official biography describes several years of club involvement and labels the management roles honorary. Exact dates are not given.
career_spells.counting_note: Honorary and volunteer community roles are excluded.

career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography lists a former presidency but supplies no dates, remuneration or workload.
career_spells.counting_note: Nonprofit governance is excluded pending evidence of separate substantive paid employment.

career_spells.role: Member of the House of Representatives for Fisher
career_spells.evidence_note: Official parliamentary records show Wallace was elected to the House of Representatives at the 2 July 2016 federal election.

research_notes: Identify the Pallottine formation dates and whether any paid work occurred; current evidence supports only excluded religious study.
Identify the apprenticeship employer and exact commencement/completion, hours and leave, followed by the subcontracting and building-business entities, licences, workload and boundaries.

Resolve why the Parliamentary Handbook records carpenter-and-joiner/builder activity through 2016 despite the described transition to 16 years at the bar in 2000; do not double-count overlapping self-employment.
Obtain QUT enrolment and graduation dates and quantify the overlap between full-time study and building-business work.
Obtain exact bar admission/cessation, chambers or practice name, workload, leave and campaign arrangements; identify the three Queensland Government reports and contracting periods.
Resolve appointment, cessation and remuneration for surf-lifesaving and Children's Therapy Centre roles.
